# Kanban Task Board with Button-Based Reordering (Reflex)

## Background

Build a Kanban-style task board as a full-stack web app using the https://reflex.dev Python framework. The board has three fixed columns rendered left-to-right: **To Do**, **Doing**, and **Done**. Each column holds an ordered list of cards. Cards are persisted in a local SQLite database with an explicit integer ordering index, and users reorder cards using buttons only (no drag-and-drop), so behavior is fully deterministic.

## Requirements

* A single page at route `/` renders the three columns side by side with their cards, ordered from top to bottom.
* Cards are stored in SQLite using a Reflex database model (`rx.Model`, `table=True`). Each card record has at least these fields:
  * `title`: the card text (string).
  * `status`: which column the card is in, one of exactly `"todo"`, `"doing"`, `"done"`.
  * `position`: a 0-based integer ordering index that is **contiguous within each column** (a column with N cards uses positions `0..N-1`, with no gaps or duplicates), and cards are displayed in ascending `position` order within their column.
* The first time the app loads and the card table is empty, seed it (once) with exactly these cards, in this order per column:
  * To Do: `Write spec` (position 0), `Design schema` (position 1), `Draft tests` (position 2)
  * Doing: `Build API` (position 0), `Wire UI` (position 1)
  * Done: `Kickoff meeting` (position 0)
* Each card provides four move buttons implemented as server-side event handlers that take the card's database id as an argument:
  * **Move right**: advance the card one column along the order `todo -> doing -> done`. Remove it from its current column (compacting the remaining cards so their positions stay contiguous) and append it to the end of the target column (its new position equals the number of cards already in the target column). If the card is already in `done`, this is a no-op.
  * **Move left**: the mirror of move right along `done -> doing -> todo`; append to the end of the target column. If already in `todo`, it is a no-op.
  * **Move up**: swap the card's position with the card directly above it in the same column. If the card is already at the top (position 0), it is a no-op.
  * **Move down**: swap the card's position with the card directly below it in the same column. If the card is already at the bottom of its column, it is a no-op.
* Every move must update the SQLite ordering indexes inside a single database session/transaction and commit the change so it persists across page reloads and server restarts. After any move, the positions in every affected column must remain a contiguous, gap-free 0-based sequence.
* Show a live per-column card count for each column, computed on the backend using Reflex computed vars (`@rx.var`). The counts must update reactively after every move.

## Implementation Hints

* Use `uv` to manage the Python environment. Initialize the project non-interactively, e.g. `uv init`, `uv add reflex`, `uv run reflex init --template blank`, then set up the database schema with `uv run reflex db init`, `uv run reflex db makemigrations --message "initial schema"`, and `uv run reflex db migrate`. Commit the generated migration files so the schema can be recreated on a fresh database.
* Persist data with `rx.Model` and perform reads/writes inside `rx.session()`; wrap each reorder in one transaction and call `commit()`.
* Derive the per-column counts with cached computed vars and render the card lists with `rx.foreach` (one foreach per column).
* Reorder handlers should accept the card id as an event argument (bind with a lambda or partial event args), mutate the DB, then reload the state's card list from the database so the UI and computed vars refresh.
* The database is the default local SQLite database (`sqlite:///reflex.db`) created in the project directory; no external services, network calls, or secrets are involved.
* Project path: `/home/user/task_board`
* Start command (run from the project path): `uv run reflex run`
* Ports: frontend on `3000`, backend on `8000`.

### Frontend contract (required so the UI can be verified)

The rendered page MUST expose the following stable hooks:

* Per-column count element: an element with attribute `data-testid` equal to `count-todo`, `count-doing`, and `count-done` respectively, whose visible text is exactly the integer count of cards in that column.
* Each card's four move buttons must set `data-testid` to, respectively, `move-left-<id>`, `move-right-<id>`, `move-up-<id>`, and `move-down-<id>`, where `<id>` is that card's database primary-key id. (Set custom attributes on the components, e.g. via `custom_attrs`.)
* Each card must also display its `title` text somewhere in the card.

### Cleanup

This app runs a development server in the background during your work. Before you finish, you MUST stop/kill every background server or process you started (both the Reflex frontend on port 3000 and backend on port 8000) so that no server is left running after your task is complete. The verifier will start its own server.

class ModelRegistry:
        """Registry for all models.

        Attributes:
            _metadata: Cache the metadata to avoid re-creating it.
        """

        models: ClassVar[set[SQLModelOrSqlAlchemy]] = set()

        _metadata: ClassVar[sqlalchemy.MetaData | None] = None

        @classmethod
        def register(cls, model: SQLModelOrSqlAlchemyT) -> SQLModelOrSqlAlchemyT:
            """Register a model. Can be used directly or as a decorator.

            Args:
                model: The model to register.

            Returns:
                The model passed in as an argument (Allows decorator usage)
            """
            cls.models.add(model)
            return model

        @classmethod
        def get_models(cls, include_empty: bool = False) -> set[SQLModelOrSqlAlchemy]:
            """Get registered models.

            Args:
                include_empty: If True, include models with empty metadata.

            Returns:
                The registered models.
            """
            if include_empty:
                return cls.models
            return {
                model for model in cls.models if not cls._model_metadata_is_empty(model)
            }

        @staticmethod
        def _model_metadata_is_empty(model: SQLModelOrSqlAlchemy) -> bool:
            """Check if the model metadata is empty.

            Args:
                model: The model to check.

            Returns:
                True if the model metadata is empty, False otherwise.
            """
            return len(model.metadata.tables) == 0

        @classmethod
        def get_metadata(cls) -> sqlalchemy.MetaData:
            """Get the database metadata.

            Returns:
                The database metadata.
            """
            if cls._metadata is not None:
                return cls._metadata

            models = cls.get_models(include_empty=False)

            if len(models) == 1:
                metadata = next(iter(models)).metadata
            else:
                # Merge the metadata from all the models.
                # This allows mixing bare sqlalchemy models with sqlmodel models in one database.
                metadata = sqlalchemy.MetaData()
                for model in cls.get_models():
                    for table in model.metadata.tables.values():
                        table.to_metadata(metadata)

            # Cache the metadata
            cls._metadata = metadata

"""Kanban task board built with Reflex."""

from __future__ import annotations

import reflex as rx

from rxconfig import config

from task_board.models import Card


# Column ordering used to decide left/right moves.
COLUMN_ORDER: tuple[str, ...] = ("todo", "doing", "done")

# Human readable labels for the columns.
COLUMN_LABELS: dict[str, str] = {
    "todo": "To Do",
    "doing": "Doing",
    "done": "Done",
}


def _next_column(status: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the column that follows ``status`` in COLUMN_ORDER, or None."""
    if status not in COLUMN_ORDER:
        return None
    idx = COLUMN_ORDER.index(status)
    if idx + 1 >= len(COLUMN_ORDER):
        return None
    return COLUMN_ORDER[idx + 1]


def _previous_column(status: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the column that precedes ``status`` in COLUMN_ORDER, or None."""
    if status not in COLUMN_ORDER:
        return None
    idx = COLUMN_ORDER.index(status)
    if idx - 1 < 0:
        return None
    return COLUMN_ORDER[idx - 1]


def _seed_if_empty() -> None:
    """Seed the database with the initial card layout on first run.

    The seeding runs inside a single database session so the whole layout
    is created atomically. Subsequent calls are a no-op because we only seed
    when there are no cards at all.
    """
    with rx.session() as session:
        existing = session.exec(Card.select()).first()
        if existing is not None:
            return

        seed_cards: list[Card] = [
            Card(title="Write spec", status="todo", position=0),
            Card(title="Design schema", status="todo", position=1),
            Card(title="Draft tests", status="todo", position=2),
            Card(title="Build API", status="doing", position=0),
            Card(title="Wire UI", status="doing", position=1),
            Card(title="Kickoff meeting", status="done", position=0),
        ]
        for card in seed_cards:
            session.add(card)
        session.commit()


class State(rx.State):
    """Top-level app state for the Kanban board."""

    # List of all cards in display order, grouped by status.
    cards: list[dict] = []

    @rx.event
    def on_load(self) -> None:
        """Load the cards from the database, seeding if needed."""
        _seed_if_empty()
        self._reload_cards()

    def _reload_cards(self) -> None:
        """Re-read the cards from the database into the state."""
        with rx.session() as session:
            rows = session.exec(
                Card.select().order_by(Card.status, Card.position)
            ).all()
        self.cards = [
            {
                "id": row.id,
                "title": row.title,
                "status": row.status,
                "position": row.position,
            }
            for row in rows
        ]

    @rx.var
    def todo_cards(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Cards that should appear in the To Do column."""
        return [c for c in self.cards if c["status"] == "todo"]

    @rx.var
    def doing_cards(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Cards that should appear in the Doing column."""
        return [c for c in self.cards if c["status"] == "doing"]

    @rx.var
    def done_cards(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Cards that should appear in the Done column."""
        return [c for c in self.cards if c["status"] == "done"]

    @rx.var
    def count_todo(self) -> int:
        """Number of cards currently in the To Do column."""
        return len(self.todo_cards)

    @rx.var
    def count_doing(self) -> int:
        """Number of cards currently in the Doing column."""
        return len(self.doing_cards)

    @rx.var
    def count_done(self) -> int:
        """Number of cards currently in the Done column."""
        return len(self.done_cards)

    @rx.event
    def move_right(self, card_id: int) -> None:
        """Move a card one column to the right (todo -> doing -> done).

        The card is removed from its current column (compacting positions so
        the remaining cards stay contiguous starting at 0) and appended to
        the end of the target column. If the card is already in the
        rightmost column, this is a no-op.
        """
        with rx.session() as session:
            card = session.get(Card, card_id)
            if card is None:
                return
            target = _next_column(card.status)
            if target is None:
                # Already in the rightmost column; nothing to do.
                session.commit()
                return

            # Compact the source column (everything after the card moves up).
            source_cards = session.exec(
                Card.select()
                .where(Card.status == card.status)
                .where(Card.position > card.position)
            ).all()
            for sibling in source_cards:
                sibling.position -= 1

            # Append the card to the end of the target column.
            target_cards = session.exec(
                Card.select().where(Card.status == target)
            ).all()
            card.status = target
            card.position = len(target_cards)
            session.add(card)
            session.commit()

        self._reload_cards()

    @rx.event
    def move_left(self, card_id: int) -> None:
        """Move a card one column to the left (done -> doing -> todo).

        The card is removed from its current column (compacting positions so
        the remaining cards stay contiguous starting at 0) and appended to
        the end of the target column. If the card is already in the
        leftmost column, this is a no-op.
        """
        with rx.session() as session:
            card = session.get(Card, card_id)
            if card is None:
                return
            target = _previous_column(card.status)
            if target is None:
                # Already in the leftmost column; nothing to do.
                session.commit()
                return

            # Compact the source column (everything after the card moves up).
            source_cards = session.exec(
                Card.select()
                .where(Card.status == card.status)
                .where(Card.position > card.position)
            ).all()
            for sibling in source_cards:
                sibling.position -= 1

            # Append the card to the end of the target column.
            target_cards = session.exec(
                Card.select().where(Card.status == target)
            ).all()
            card.status = target
            card.position = len(target_cards)
            session.add(card)
            session.commit()

        self._reload_cards()

    @rx.event
    def move_up(self, card_id: int) -> None:
        """Swap a card with the one directly above it in the same column.

        If the card is already at the top (position 0) this is a no-op.
        """
        with rx.session() as session:
            card = session.get(Card, card_id)
            if card is None:
                return
            if card.position == 0:
                session.commit()
                return

            above = session.exec(
                Card.select()
                .where(Card.status == card.status)
                .where(Card.position == card.position - 1)
            ).first()
            if above is None:
                # No card directly above; nothing to swap.
                session.commit()
                return

            # Swap positions.
            card.position, above.position = above.position, card.position
            session.add(card)
            session.add(above)
            session.commit()

        self._reload_cards()

    @rx.event
    def move_down(self, card_id: int) -> None:
        """Swap a card with the one directly below it in the same column.

        If the card is already at the bottom of its column this is a no-op.
        """
        with rx.session() as session:
            card = session.get(Card, card_id)
            if card is None:
                return
            below = session.exec(
                Card.select()
                .where(Card.status == card.status)
                .where(Card.position == card.position + 1)
            ).first()
            if below is None:
                # No card directly below; nothing to swap.
                session.commit()
                return

            # Swap positions.
            card.position, below.position = below.position, card.position
            session.add(card)
            session.add(below)
            session.commit()

        self._reload_cards()


def _card_view(card: dict) -> rx.Component:
    """Render a single card with its title and the four move buttons."""
    card_id = card["id"]
    return rx.box(
        rx.text(card["title"], font_weight="bold", margin_bottom="0.5em"),
        rx.hstack(
            rx.button(
                "Left",
                on_click=State.move_left(card_id),
                custom_attrs={"data-testid": f"move-left-{card_id}"},
                size="1",
            ),
            rx.button(
                "Right",
                on_click=State.move_right(card_id),
                custom_attrs={"data-testid": f"move-right-{card_id}"},
                size="1",
            ),
            rx.button(
                "Up",
                on_click=State.move_up(card_id),
                custom_attrs={"data-testid": f"move-up-{card_id}"},
                size="1",
            ),
            rx.button(
                "Down",
                on_click=State.move_down(card_id),
                custom_attrs={"data-testid": f"move-down-{card_id}"},
                size="1",
            ),
            spacing="1",
        ),
        border="1px solid #ccc",
        border_radius="6px",
        padding="0.75em",
        margin_bottom="0.5em",
        background="#fafafa",
        width="100%",
    )


def _column_view(status: str, title: str, testid: str) -> rx.Component:
    """Render a single column: a heading, a count badge, and the card list."""
    if status == "todo":
        cards_var = State.todo_cards
    elif status == "doing":
        cards_var = State.doing_cards
